say_en: The Cat at the Door
show_en: The Cat at the Door

say_en: This is Mina. She is nine. Mina has a mother, a father and a small brother. Her house is in a village. It is a small house with a brown door. Every morning Mina opens the door and looks at the sun.
show_en: This is Mina. She is nine. Mina has a mother, a father and a small brother. Her house is in a village. It is a small house with a brown door. Every morning Mina opens the door and looks at the sun.

say_en: One morning a cat is at the door. It is a small orange cat. The cat looks at Mina. "Miaow," says the cat. "Hello, cat," says Mina. "Are you hungry?" Yes, the cat is very hungry.
show_en: One morning a cat is at the door. It is a small orange cat. The cat looks at Mina. "Miaow," says the cat. "Hello, cat," says Mina. "Are you hungry?" Yes, the cat is very hungry.

say_en: Mina has bread in her hand. It is her breakfast. She gives the bread to the cat. The cat eats and eats. Now Mina has no bread, but she is happy. "You are my friend," she says to the cat.
show_en: Mina has bread in her hand. It is her breakfast. She gives the bread to the cat. The cat eats and eats. Now Mina has no bread, but she is happy. "You are my friend," she says to the cat.

show_en: The Fox and the Grapes

say_en: This is a fox. He is orange and white, and he has a big tail. The fox is not happy today. He is hungry and he has no food. He walks and walks. He looks in the field. No food. He looks at the river. No food.
show_en: This is a fox. He is orange and white, and he has a big tail. The fox is not happy today. He is hungry and he has no food. He walks and walks. He looks in the field. No food. He looks at the river. No food.

say_en: Then the fox comes to a garden. In the garden he sees green leaves. And look! Grapes! They are big grapes. "I like grapes," says the fox. "I am very hungry. These grapes are my food today!"
show_en: Then the fox comes to a garden. In the garden he sees green leaves. And look! Grapes! They are big grapes. "I like grapes," says the fox. "I am very hungry. These grapes are my food today!"

say_en: The grapes are high up.
show_en: The grapes are high up.

say_en: But the grapes are high. They are very high up. The fox stands on two legs. He opens his mouth. No. He can't touch the grapes. "I can jump," says the fox. He jumps. One, two, three! No. The grapes are too high.

say_en: The fox goes back. He runs and he jumps. He jumps again and again. Four, five, six times! Now his legs are tired and his nose is hot. But the grapes are high and the fox is small. He can't have them.
show_en: The fox goes back. He runs and he jumps. He jumps again and again. Four, five, six times! Now his legs are tired and his nose is hot. But the grapes are high and the fox is small. He can't have them.

say_en: The fox sits down. He looks at the grapes. He is sad and he is hungry. Then he stands up. "I don't like these grapes," he says. "They are green. They are not sweet. They are bad grapes. I don't want them!"
show_en: The fox sits down. He looks at the grapes. He is sad and he is hungry. Then he stands up. "I don't like these grapes," he says. "They are green. They are not sweet. They are bad grapes. I don't want them!"

say_en: The fox walks away with his nose up. But a small bird in the tree sees it all. "The grapes are good," says the bird. "The fox can't have them. So he says: They are bad." The bird eats a grape. It is very sweet.

show_en: Are the grapes bad?

intro_fa: حمید یک نهال بسیار خُرد دارد و هر روز آن را آب می‌دهد. آیا از آن یک درخت کلان جور می‌شود؟

show_en: Hamid's Tree

say_en: Hamid is ten. One day his grandfather gives him a very small tree. It has four leaves. "This is an apple tree," says Grandfather. "Give it water. One day it can give you apples." Hamid looks at the small tree. "This? Apples?"
show_en: Hamid is ten. One day his grandfather gives him a very small tree. It has four leaves. "This is an apple tree," says Grandfather. "Give it water. One day it can give you apples." Hamid looks at the small tree. "This? Apples?"

say_en: Hamid puts the tree in the garden. Every morning he goes to the well. He comes back with a bucket of water. The bucket is big and Hamid is small. But every morning he gives water to his tree. "Good morning, tree," he says.
show_en: Hamid puts the tree in the garden. Every morning he goes to the well. He comes back with a bucket of water. The bucket is big and Hamid is small. But every morning he gives water to his tree. "Good morning, tree," he says.

show_en: His friends come with a ball. "Come and play, Hamid!" "I can't," says Hamid. "My tree is thirsty." The friends laugh. "That is not a tree. It is a stick with four leaves!" Hamid is sad. But he goes to the well.

say_en: Then summer comes. The sun is very hot. There is no rain. The leaves of the small tree are yellow. One leaf falls down. Then two. "Please, tree, be green again," says Hamid. Now he goes to the well two times every day.

show_en: One year. Two years. Three years. Hamid is thirteen now, and the tree is big. It is green and it has white flowers. Then the flowers go, and Hamid sees small green apples. He counts them: "Ten, twenty, thirty... a hundred apples!"

show_en: Jawad and the Old Donkey

say_en: Jawad is eleven. Every morning he gets up at five o'clock. He takes two big cans and walks to the well. The well is far from his house. Then he walks home with the water. The cans are very heavy.
show_en: Jawad is eleven. Every morning he gets up at five o'clock. He takes two big cans and walks to the well. The well is far from his house. Then he walks home with the water. The cans are very heavy.

say_en: Jawad's arms are tired. His legs are tired. At eight o'clock he goes to school. He sits down and opens his book. But his eyes close. "Jawad!" says the teacher. "Are you sleeping?" "Sorry, teacher," says Jawad.
show_en: Jawad's arms are tired. His legs are tired. At eight o'clock he goes to school. He sits down and opens his book. But his eyes close. "Jawad!" says the teacher. "Are you sleeping?" "Sorry, teacher," says Jawad.
